This Appeal, Coming On For Admission, This Day
Rajesh Rai K J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the Insurance Company against the judgment and award dated 19.07.2019 passed by the Additional MACT and Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar, sitting at Bhalki,
in MVC No.340/2014, wherein the Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition filed by the respondents/claimants and awarded compensation of Rs.16,96,000/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its deposit.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bidar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.
The facts giving rise to filing of this appeal are that respondent No.1 is the claimant No.1 is the wife and claimant Nos.2 to 5 are the children and claimant No.6 is the mother of deceased Balaji.
On 09.02.2014 said Balaji along with his friend Sanjay Salunke was proceeding on Royal Enfield Bullet motorcycle bearing registration No.MH-23/AG-4216 from Maslga Village to Tulajapur.
Sanjay was riding the motorcycle and Balaji was a pillion rider.

When they came near hotel Magh Malhar within the limits of Kakramba village, a street dog suddenly came in front of the vehicle and rider could not control his motorcycle and skidded on the road, as a result, both of them fell on the road and sustained injuries.
Balaji, sustained fatal injuries over his head and he succumbed to the said injuries on the spot itself.

Thereafter, the first information was registered before the Tulajapur police station and a case in Crime No.34/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 337,
304-A of IPC was registered.

As such, the claimants filed the claim petition NC:
2024:KHC-K:3866-DB under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of deceased Balaji in the road traffic accident.
4. After service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 have entered appearance i.e, appellant herein and filed the statement of objections by denying the averments of the claim petition.
After perusal of the claim petition so also the statement of objections filed by the appellant herein, the Tribunal framed the relevant issues and recorded the evidence.
In order to prove the case, the petitioners examined petitioner No.1 as PW.1 and got marked the documents as Exs.P1 to P10.

The Insurance Company examined its Assistant Manager (Legal) as RW.1 and got marked the documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
5.

After assessment of oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal allowed the claim petition in The Divisional Manager vs Anita And Ors on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151262267/
3 part and awarded compensation as stated supra.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Anita And Ors on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further held that the respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation amount and directed the respondent No.2/Insurance Company to pay the NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB compensation amount.
Being aggrieved by fastening of liability, respondent No.2/Insurance Company is before this Court.
6. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellant/respondent No.2/Insurance Company and the learned counsel for the respondents/claimants.

7. It is the primary contention of the learned counsel for the respondent No.2/Insurance Company that the Tribunal totally erred while allowing the claim petition by fastening the liability on the Insurance Company so also by granting compensation.

According to the learned counsel, the Tribunal failed to appreciate that the insured vehicle Royal Enfield Bullet bearing registration No.MH- 23/AG-4216 was falsely implicated in the accident as the deceased Balaji was a pillion rider and the rider of the said vehicle said to have sustained injuries due to the alleged accident.

Though application was filed for production of documents from the concerned police station in respect of rider of the vehicle and for investigation officer to prove NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB the fact that rider also sustained injuries, the said application came to be dismissed by the Tribunal.
As such, the Tribunal also not provided sufficient opportunity to prove the case of Insurance Company.
She further contends that the Tribunal erred in taking the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/-, as no such document was placed by the claimants to prove the income of the deceased.
She also contends that the Tribunal erroneously taken 40% of the income for future prospects since deceased was aged about 54 years at the time of accident.
Hence, the same is against the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: She further contends that the Tribunal has awarded exorbitant compensation under all other heads.
Hence, on these grounds, she prays to allow the appeal.

8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the respondents/claimants submit that the Tribunal after NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB considering the evidence and documents placed before it, rightly allowed the claim petition and reasonably awarded compensation under all other heads.

He would further contend that the accident is not in dispute since the claimants have placed documents Ex.P.1 to P.7 which clearly depicts that the jurisdictional police registered the case against the rider of the offending motorcycle which was insured by the appellant herein.
Nonetheless, the PME report and MLC information clearly reveal that the deceased has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident caused due to fall from Bullet motorcycle.
In such circumstance, the Tribunal has rightly answered issues and awarded compensation under different heads.
He would further contend that the Tribunal has rightly taken into consideration the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month and awarded future prospects.
Hence, he submits that the impugned judgment does not call for interference by this Court.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the appeal.

Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties so also having perused the material available on record, the points that would arise for our consideration are:
The Divisional Manager vs Anita And Ors on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151262267/
4 i.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Whether the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is required to be interfered with by this Court?
ii. What Order?
10. In order to prove the accident, as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the respondents that the respondents/claimants have produced 10 documents namely Ex.P.1 to P.10.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR and Ex.P.2 is the crime details form and these two documents clearly reveal that the accident in question occurred on 09.02.2014 near Megha Malhar Hotel within the limits of Karkamba village.
Further Ex.P.3 inquest panchanama and Ex.P.4 PME report also depicts that the deceased died due to road traffic accident.
After investigation of the case, the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet.

Admittedly the - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB appellant herein failed to get examine any witness, including the rider of the motorcycle and also failed to challenge the charge sheet laid by the jurisdictional police.

In such circumstance, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited vs. Smt.Lakshmamma and Others in the case of MFA NO.7493/2007 disposed of on 25.09.2007 held in para No.6 which reads as under:
6.

entities.text: Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Limited vs. Smt.Lakshmamma and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Then, coming to the question of involvement of the vehicle, admittedly charge- sheet is filed against the driver of the vehicle, the owner has not denied the accident.
FIR is registered in Crime No.10/05 by the Malur Police.

If really the vehicle was not involved, if a false case has been lodged and if the owner has colluded with the claimants, it was for the insurance company to challenge the same to quash the charge-sheet and to direct the police to investigate properly and file an appropriate case for having lodged a false case when there was no accident and vehicle in question had not been involved.

The learned counsel for the appellant submits that after case was filed, the - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB matter was entrusted to a private agency for investigation and accordingly to the report of the investigation of a private agency, the vehicle in question had not been involved in the accident.

But, we cannot place reliance on a report submitted by a private agency when a charge- sheet is filed by the police after a detailed investigation and when the driver and owner of the vehicle have not disputed about the involvement of the vehicle in question.

Therefore, this point is also answered against the appellant."
11.
On perusal of the above judgment, we find that it squarely applies to the facts and circumstances of the present case.

Hence, the Tribunal rightly held that the death has caused due to rash and The Divisional Manager vs Anita And Ors on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151262267/
5 negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle and accordingly, rightly fastened the liability on the respondent No.2-Insurance Company.
12.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Anita And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Insofar as quantum is concerned, we have carefully examined the judgment passed by the Tribunal

wherein the Tribunal considering the income of the deceased at Rs.10,000/- per month which is just and - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB proper since the same is to be taken into consideration after considering the RTC extracts produced by him as per Ex.P.8 i.e. the licence issued by the panchayat authority which depicts that the deceased was running a Grocery shop.

To the aforesaid amount, as the deceased was aged 54 years, 10% of the said amount has to be added on account of future prospects,
in view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra).
Thus, the monthly income comes to Rs.11,000/-.

Out of which, considering that there are 6 dependents, we deem it appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the said income towards personal expenses of the deceased and therefore, the monthly income of the deceased comes to Rs.8,250/-.

Taking into account the age of the deceased which was 54 years at the time of accident, multiplier of '11' has to be adopted as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioners are - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB entitled to a sum of Rs.10,89,000/- (8250*12*11) on account of loss of dependency.
13. Further the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation under the head loss of consortium at Rs.2,80,000/- and compensation towards loss of estate and funeral expenses at Rs.30,000/-.
Hence, the same is retained.

14. Thus, in all, the petitioners are entitled to a sum of Rs.13,99,000/- as against Rs.16,96,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

15. In view of the above discussion, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is modified.

iii. The petitioners are entitled to total compensation of Rs.13,99,000/- as against Rs.16,96,000/- along with interest at the - 14 - The Divisional Manager vs Anita And Ors on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151262267/
6 NC: 2024:KHC-K:3866-DB rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
iv.

vi. Amount in deposit, if any, be transferred to the Tribunal.
